title: Role of inflammatory markers and response to energy and protein delivery in critically ill patients, a pilot, proof-of-concept, prospective observational study
summary: Nutrition therapy is considered an integral part of the treatment of critically ill patients in the intensive care unit and has an impact on the clinical course of the illness. A patient’s metabolism and immune system continuously change during severe illness and may influence the patient’s response to different therapies. For patient nutrition, this relationship has not yet been investigated. This study examines whether the patient’s response to nutrition can be better understood based on specific inflammatory markers in the blood. For this purpose, these markers will be measured through blood samples during the first two weeks in the intensive care unit. Participation in the study has no influence on the patients’ treatment.
conditions: Interaction between inflammatory markers and clinical nutrition in critically ill patients

interventions.name: Observation group: Patients over 18 years of age, on mechanical ventilation, and with an expected ICU stay of at least 4 days at the time of study enrollment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Mechanical ventilation
Expected ICU stay of 4 or more days
Exclusion criteria:
Moribund condition or expected withdrawal of life-sustaining measures within the next 24 hours

Expected lack of consent for study participation based on the known wishes of the patient, or refusal by the patient or legal representative
